newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Second senior North Korea military leader dies.
newsitem.headline: Second senior North Korea military leader dies.

text.p: North Korea's vice-defence minister Kim Kwang-jin died on Thursday, less than a week after the death of the defence minister, monitoring agencies reported.
The demise in quick succession of the two top figures in the communist nation's powerful armed forces comes on top of other leadership upheavals.
Earlier this month, North Korea's Prime Minister was replaced -- apparently for health reasons -- and its chief ideologue defected to a South Korean diplomatic mission in Beijing.

Kim Kwang-jin, first vice-minister of the North Korean People's Armed Forces, died aged 69 of "incurable sickness", the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) on Friday quoted Pyongyang radio as reporting.
He was also a member of the Central Committee of the ruling Workers' Party.
The funeral will be held on Saturday, the radio reported.
Kim's superior, Choe Kwang, died of a heart attack last Friday, North Korean official media reported.

Cracks are appearing in North Korea's secretive power structure as top leader Kim Jong-il prepares to formally assume the titles of state president and Worker's Party general secretary left vacant by the death of his father, the "Great Leader" Kim Il-sung, in 1994.
North Korea watchers believe the younger Kim will complete the socialist world's first dynastic succession around the time of the third anniversary of his father's death in July.
Defector Hwang Jang-yop is still holed up at Seoul's consular office in the Chinese capital after arriving there with an aide on February 12.
South Korean efforts to persuade China to allow Hwang safe passage to Seoul have so far produced no progress.
